sentence: We present the case of a 29-year-old male (165 cm, 68 kg), Afghan police officer, who during an attack suffered open trauma to the right elbow secondary to the impact of a firearm (probably 7.62 mm AK-74). ).

After the incident, a humeral tourniquet was placed, a granulated hemostatic agent was applied topically (Celox® SAM Medical Products, Newport, Oregon, USA) and tranexamic acid (1 g iv) was administered.
He was evacuated by means of a medical helicopter to the Spanish Role 2E in Herat (Afghanistan), arriving at the triage room 70 minutes after suffering the injury.

In the primary assessment, the injured man had GCS 15 pts, peripheral SatO2 of 98%, heart rate of 110 bpm, non-invasive blood pressure of 130/80 mmHg and good pain control (VAS 2/10) after administration of midazolam ( 3 mg iv) and ketamine (30 mg iv).
The presence of a gunshot wound with an entry hole in the elbow without an exit hole was confirmed.
The radiograph revealed a distal fracture of the left humerus, a proximal fracture of the left ulna, and a proximal fracture of the left radius.
Surgical intervention was decided for debridement, cleaning, removal of bone chips and placement of an external fixator in the left arm under general anesthesia.
During the preanesthetic study, no significant alterations were found in the blood tests, ECG, or airway assessment.
The patient did not remember when his last intake had been and accepted informed consent in the presence of an interpreter.

In the operating room, grade I monitoring was used (peripheral SatO2, heart rate, non-invasive blood pressure and capnography) augmented with a bispectral analysis device (BIS®), continuous hemoglobin monitor (Masimo® Radical 7) and oropharyngeal thermometer.
The casualty was premedicated with midazolam (1 mg IV) and ketamine (20 mg IV).

After 3 minutes of denitrogenization with 80% FiO2, achieving a SatO2 of 100%, rapid sequence anesthetic induction was carried out with fentanyl (150 μg iv), propofol (130 mg iv) and rocuronium (30 mg iv).
Standard laryngoscopy (Cormak II) was performed, the airway was isolated with a 7.5 mm endotracheal tube, and the pneumotamponade balloon was filled with air (8 ml).
After selecting protective ventilation parameters (VT 420 ml, PEEP 7, FiO2 45%), it was not necessary to perform alveolar recruitment maneuvers.
Anesthetic maintenance was performed with a mixture of O2, air and sevoflurane.
During the 75 minutes of the surgical procedure, the patient remained prone to tachycardia.

The intervention performed was open reduction under scopic control, transarticular osteosynthesis through implantation of a Hoffmann II Stryker external fixator in a multiplanar configuration, pulsatile lavage of the wound and debridement of the necrotic tissue involving the extesor carpi ulnaris, flexor carpi ulnaris and triceps tendon.

Antitetanus, antibiotic (cefazolin 2 g iv and metronidazole 500 mg iv), gastroprotective (omeprazole 40 mg iv), antiemetic (granisetron 3 mg iv), anti-inflammatory (desketoprofen 50 mg iv), ocular (oculos-epithelializing ointment together with forced eyelid closure), orthopedic (joint protection) and thermal (regulation of operating room temperature, fluid heater and hot air blanket).

To improve pain control, in addition to performing multimodal analgesia (metamizole 2 g iv, paracetamol 1 g iv, ketamine 30 mg iv and fentanyl 150 μg iv), an ultrasound-guided peripheral nerve block was used at the interscalene level using 37 mg of bupivacaine 0 .25%.
Eduction was uneventful and neither opioid antagonization nor muscle relaxant reversal was necessary.
The patient was admitted stable and with good pain control to the intensive care unit and later transferred to the hospital ward.
He was discharged from Role 2E 72 hours after suffering the attack, being evacuated to an Afghan military hospital for healing of soft parts and future osteosynthesis.
